name: codex-hook-trust-format
purpose: How Codex identifies and hashes a per-launch hook entry (-c hooks.<Event>=[...]) for hooks.state trust (RN-5). For internal/spawn/testdata/. Verified against Codex's own hooks/list on 0.156.0, 0.159.2 and 0.162.1 (identical): 633 listed entries (211 per version), 0 mismatches with golden/recompute.py.

key.sourceNote: the literal string, angle brackets included: the synthetic config layer that -c / --config flags form
key.groupIndex: 0-based position of the matcher group inside the event's array (hooks.<Event>=[ {group}, {group} ])
key.handlerIndex: 0-based position of the handler inside the group's hooks array
key.stateSetting: -c 'hooks.state={"<key>"={trusted_hash="sha256:<hex>"},...}'  (inline-table form; the table merges across config layers)

identity.description: The JSON object that is hashed: one per HANDLER (not per group). Its fields, after normalisation:

fields.event_name: the event label (snake_case, as in the key); always present
fields.matcher: present only when the group has a matcher AND the event takes one; omitted otherwise. The empty string counts as a matcher (it hashes differently from none)
fields.hooks: an array of exactly ONE handler object: {type, command, timeout, async} plus optional additionalContextLimit

handlerFields.command: the command string exactly as given in the -c value (after TOML decoding), byte for byte
handlerFields.timeout: integer seconds, ALWAYS present: the value given, or the default when none given (see normalisation)
handlerFields.additionalContextLimit: present only when the setting is given, is not 2500, and the event honours it (see normalisation)
handlerFields.statusMessage: present only when set (AD does not set it; not probed here)

normalisation.timeoutClamp: SessionEnd and Interrupt: the value is clamped into 1..3 (0 -> 1, 600 -> 3; Codex logs 'clamping <Event> hook timeout to 3s'). Other events: the value as given (RN-9: no cap; hooks/list timeoutSec equals the value given, e.g. the 86400 relay window). Values <= 0 on other events were not probed
normalisation.helpEntryTimeout: the help entry passes no timeout, so it hashes timeout 600 (SessionStart)
normalisation.matcherDropped: UserPromptSubmit, Stop and Interrupt ignore a matcher: it is not hashed (Stop with matcher '*' hashes like Stop with none). PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest hash it when set ('*' and 'Bash' and '' each give a different hash from none)

additionalContextLimit.ignoredBy: every other event: not hashed (Codex logs 'ignoring additionalContextLimit for <Event> hook'; Stop with limit 4000 hashes like Stop with none)
additionalContextLimit.defaultNotHashed: a value of exactly 2500 (Codex's default) is left out: hashes like no setting. 0, 3790, 4000 and 100000 are all hashed (each its own hash)

serialisation.form: compact JSON, object keys sorted ascending at every level, separators ',' and ':' with no spaces, non-ASCII characters written as themselves (not \uXXXX escaped), UTF-8

hash.algorithm: SHA-256 over the serialised UTF-8 bytes
hash.listedAs: hooks/list currentHash; the value to put in hooks.state trusted_hash
hash.trustedWhen: hooks.state[<key>].trusted_hash equals currentHash: hooks/list reports trustStatus 'trusted', no 'Hooks need review' dialog, and the hook runs, with NO --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust

commandForms.quoting: SR-5.3: the path goes inside single quotes; each ' is written '\'' and each \ is written '\\'
commandForms.hook: exec <quoted binary path> hook --agent codex      (PermissionRequest: ... --agent codex --timeout <relay window seconds>)

adEntries.matcher: none on every event (RN-15: no matcher is the recommended form)
adEntries.noCompactionHelpEntry: no hook on PreCompact or PostCompact (RN-3)

rn15.choice: no matcher on PreToolUse, PostToolUse and PermissionRequest
rn15.why: Same behaviour as '*' (RN-15: both match every tool on all three versions), one identity shape for every event (no matcher field on any entry, so the hash does not depend on a per-event matcher rule), and it is today's AD form
rn15.otherFormHash: '*' gives a DIFFERENT hash and the key is unchanged: switching forms later changes three hashes (golden scenario plain-same-group-matcher-star vs plain-same-group-limit4000)

keyStability: a hash does not depend on layout (group and handler indices are in the key only; verified for both paths); for a given layout the keys are identical on all three versions; moving the help entry from same-group to own-group changes only the help entry's key (session_start:0:1 -> session_start:1:0) and puts the AD entry alone in group 0; the help-first layouts swap the indices of the two SessionStart handlers
